---
title: "Case study: stems over topography at Wanang"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5
)
```

Forest dynamics plots such as the 50 ha Wanang plot in Papua New Guinea map
every stem in local metres (`gx`, `gy`). tidymapr draws the stems over the
plot's topography; census verbs (`stems_*()`) live in tidydiversity. The
example plot, stems and DEM below are illustrative.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidymapr)
library(tidydiversity)
library(ggplot2)
stems <- geo_example_stems()
dem <- geo_example_dem()
stems
```

## Stem map

```{r topo, fig.alt = "Stems coloured by species and sized by DBH over hillshade and contours"}
plot_topo(stems, colour = species, size = dbh, dem = dem, boundary = c(0, 0, 100, 100)) +
  labs(title = "Stems over topography", subtitle = "Illustrative ForestGEO-style plot")
```

## Terrain variables

`geo_raster_terrain()` derives slope, aspect and topographic position from
the DEM, ready for habitat classification.

```{r terrain, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
terrain <- geo_raster_terrain(dem, v = c("slope", "TPI"))
terrain
```

## Quadrats and abundance with tidydiversity

```{r quadrats}
stems |>
  stems_quadrat(grid = 20) |>
  stems_abundance(.by = quadrat)
```
